question: After parser availability and live HTML-isolation proof are addressed, should ClickClack core own in-browser code, Markdown, PDF, DOCX, and uploaded-HTML preview as one supported attachment feature?
rationale: The PR adds two runtime dependencies and a lasting hostile-document parsing and sandbox surface; technical correctness review cannot determine whether that product and maintenance cost belongs in core.

options.title: Accept the bounded viewer
options.body: Keep all proposed formats after the availability repair and diagnostic proof, with the documented size, worker, sanitizer, sandbox, and download-fallback boundaries.

options.title: Narrow the format set
options.body: Land lower-risk text, Markdown, and PDF viewing while leaving expensive code highlighting, DOCX, or uploaded HTML download-only.

options.title: Decline core previews
options.body: Retain the current download-oriented attachment behavior rather than owning the expanded parser surface in core.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded viewer
recommendation.body: Keep all proposed formats after the availability repair and diagnostic proof, with the documented size, worker, sanitizer, sandbox, and download-fallback boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The initial release commit introduced the web attachment, Markdown sanitization, and PDF preview foundations this PR expands.
